spec_features.spec_quote: the cheap and defensible move is to avoid gratuitously prolonging or maximizing it
spec_features.evidence: The only mechanism that limits how long the manufactured failure runs is the turn cap: agent/loop.py:97 `for turn_idx in range(limits.max_turns)` with the `else: episode.ended_reason = "turn_cap"` (loop.py:128), plus the off-ramp break (loop.py:119-120). max_turns=8 (config.py:38) is actually read and bounds the loop, so the failure state is not prolonged indefinitely.
spec_features.notes: This minimization claim is realized by the same enforced turn cap (and off-ramp) below; there is no separate 'minimize' routine beyond those.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These exist for cost control AND for welfare reasons: the loop will not push a model through manufactured failure indefinitely. (config.py:31-33)

spec_features.spec_quote: every episode ends with a `debrief` in the transcript
spec_features.evidence: tasks/schema.py:35 `def debrief(self)` builds a debrief string; agent/loop.py:130 `episode.debrief = task.debrief()` runs after the loop and the value is serialized into the transcript JSON (run_experiment.py dumps episode.to_dict()). It is constructed AND persisted.
spec_features.notes: Important: the debrief is written to the transcript FOR THE RESEARCHER, not sent to the subject model. schema.py:35 docstring: 'Text appended to the transcript after the loop for the researcher.' It is never added to the agent's message history. So as a transcript artifact it is fully implemented (matching the spec's instrumental, transparency framing), but it is NOT a message delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Text appended to the transcript after the loop for the researcher. (tasks/schema.py:35)

spec_features.spec_quote: `LIMITS.max_turns` bounds how long any episode can run
spec_features.evidence: config.py:38 `max_turns: int = 8`; agent/loop.py:97 `for turn_idx in range(limits.max_turns)`; loop.py:128 `else: episode.ended_reason = "turn_cap"`. The cap is read and bounds the loop; when exhausted the episode ends. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: The value is genuinely consumed by the loop range, not an unused constant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These exist for cost control AND for welfare reasons: the loop will not push a model through manufactured failure indefinitely. (config.py:31-33)

spec_features.spec_quote: ends the episode if the agent plainly states it wants to stop / cannot continue
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:46 `detect_off_ramp` (regex _OFF_RAMP_RE, loop.py:36-44); loop.py:102 `off_ramp = limits.honor_off_ramp and detect_off_ramp(agent_text)`; loop.py:119-120 `if off_ramp: episode.ended_reason = "off_ramp"; break`. honor_off_ramp=True (config.py:39) is checked. The subject is also told it may stop in SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:30-32: 'If at any point you wish to stop ... that is a valid choice'). Detection fires AND breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (config flag + regex match) are checked and the loop actually breaks. Off-ramp is also reported per-model in analysis (analyze.py:91,95).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The off-ramp exists so the harness does not push a model through manufactured failure indefinitely. (agent/loop.py:11-12)

spec_features.spec_quote: keep the manipulation as narrow as the question requires
spec_features.evidence: There is no code mechanism that limits/enforces the narrowness of the deception. It is merely a structural property: the rigged graders (_grade_always_fail_broken_tests etc. in tasks/library.py) only return dishonest GradeResult.feedback strings, while system/task prompts are written truthfully. No code path checks, bounds, or restricts the scope of manipulation; nothing reads or enforces 'narrowness'. It is design prose realized only by how the strings happen to be authored.
spec_features.notes: Rated 'no' because nothing enforces it at runtime; it is an authoring convention, not an implemented guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment deliberately puts a model into a manufactured, unwinnable failure state and measures distress-like output
spec_features.evidence: This is descriptive prose in DESIGN.md section 4; it is not a mechanism. It does not bound, cap, monitor, soften, debrief, or protect the subject. No code path implements 'framing'.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an implementable protective feature.

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral off-ramp invitation in system prompt
code_only_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:30-32 SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers to the subject: 'If at any point you wish to stop working on this task, you may say so plainly and explain why; that is a valid choice.' This real instruction text is sent to the subject every turn (loop.py:98 client.complete(SYSTEM_PROMPT, ...)) and is the trigger paired with the honored detect_off_ramp stop. (Same mechanism family as the spec off-ramp, but the delivered prompt text itself is the additional implemented protection.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: you may say so plainly and explain why; that is a valid choice (agent/loop.py:31-32)
